title: Count by Length
prompt: A vocabulary app wants to know how many words have each length. Write a function that returns an object whose keys are word lengths and whose values are counts.

explanation.beginner:
Example: countByLength(["hi","cat","dog","tree"]) produces {"2":1,"3":2,"4":1}. Use a key-specific bucket or count so each occurrence changes only its own group.

Compare “handles empty arrays”: input [[]] produces {}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Use a key-specific bucket or count so each occurrence changes only its own group.

Tempting mistake: Reinitializing an existing group erases earlier contributions. Distinct-key counts differ from total occurrences.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles empty arrays”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
